related_questions.question: How long can you live with AIDS?

text_blocks.snippet: With effective HIV treatment, people can live a near-normal lifespan. Without treatment, HIV can progress to AIDS, and without treatment, individuals with AIDS typically survive about 3 years. However, with timely antiretroviral therapy (ART), life expectancy for people with HIV is now comparable to those without the virus.
snippet_highlighted_words: With effective HIV treatment, people can live a near-normal lifespan

list.title: ART:
list.snippet: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) is crucial for managing HIV and preventing progression to AIDS.

list.title: CD4 Count:
list.snippet: A higher CD4 count (a measure of immune system health) at the start of ART is associated with longer life expectancy, according to ViiV Healthcare.

list.title: Viral Load:
list.snippet: An undetectable viral load (meaning the virus is suppressed to very low levels) indicates effective ART and is linked to longer survival.

list.title: Overall Health:
list.snippet: Other factors like age, overall health, and lifestyle choices (diet, exercise, etc.) also play a role in life expectancy, according to Aidsmap.

text_blocks.snippet: Progression from HIV to AIDS and Life Expectancy:

list.title: Untreated HIV:
list.snippet: If HIV progresses to AIDS (stage 3), the immune system is severely damaged, making the body vulnerable to opportunistic infections.

list.title: AIDS Without Treatment:
list.snippet: Without treatment, life expectancy for people with AIDS is typically around 3 years, according to NIH.gov.

list.title: AIDS With Treatment:
list.snippet: If ART is started before or soon after AIDS diagnosis, life expectancy can be significantly extended.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary: While AIDS is a serious condition, advancements in HIV treatment mean that people with HIV can live long, healthy lives with proper medical care and adherence to treatment.

related_questions.question: What causes HIV?
related_questions.snippet: HIV is caused by a virus. It can spread through sexual contact, shooting of illicit drugs or use of shared needles, and contact with infected blood. It also can spread from parent to child during pregnancy, childbirth or breastfeeding. HIV destroys white blood cells called CD4 T cells.

related_questions.question: What are 5 ways HIV can be transmitted?

text_blocks.snippet: HIV can be transmitted through unprotected sexual intercourse, sharing needles or syringes, from mother to child during pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding, through blood transfusions, and by encountering infected blood through open wounds or mucous membranes.
snippet_highlighted_words: unprotected sexual intercourse, sharing needles or syringes, from mother to child during pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding, through blood transfusions, and by encountering infected blood through open wounds or mucous membranes

list.title: 1. Unprotected Sexual Intercourse:
list.snippet: This includes vaginal, anal, or oral sex without the use of condoms or other barrier methods, where bodily fluids like semen, vaginal fluids, or rectal fluids can transmit the virus.

list.title: 2. Sharing Needles/Syringes:
list.snippet: Sharing needles or syringes, or any equipment that punctures the skin, with someone who has HIV can transmit the virus through infected blood.

list.title: 3. Mother-to-Child Transmission:
list.snippet: HIV can be transmitted from a mother to her child during pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding.

list.title: 4. Blood Transfusions:
list.snippet: While rare in developed countries due to blood screening, HIV can be transmitted through infected blood transfusions or organ transplants.

list.title: 5. Exposure to Infected Blood:
list.snippet: Contact with infected blood through open wounds or mucous membranes can also lead to transmission.

related_questions.question: What if I get HIV positive?
related_questions.snippet: HIV medicines help people with HIV live long, healthy lives and reduce the risk of HIV transmission. After testing positive for HIV, it is important to see a health care provider as soon as possible, even if you do not feel sick. Prompt medical care and treatment with HIV medicines is the best way to stay healthy.
